🧠 Project Description

This project develops an advanced, interactive dashboard that integrates sales, marketing, and inventory data to provide comprehensive insights into retail operations. Utilizing the Online Retail II dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository , the dashboard offers real-time analytics, trend analysis, and predictive insights to aid decision-making in retail management.

🧪 Example Input & Output

Input:

  • Date Range: 2010-12-01 to 2011-12-09
  • Country: United Kingdom
  • Product Category: All

Expected Output:

  • Time-series graph of sales over the selected period
  • Bar chart of top-selling products
  • Inventory turnover rates
  • Marketing campaign effectiveness metrics

🧰 Frameworks & Libraries Used

  • pandas for data manipulation
  • numpy for numerical operations
  • plotly and dash for interactive visualizations and dashboard creation
  • scikit-learn for any necessary machine learning components
  • datetime for date and time operations

🧾 Final Product Output

An interactive dashboard accessible via a web browser, featuring:

  • Dynamic filters for date range, country, and product category
  • Interactive graphs and charts displaying sales trends, inventory levels, and marketing metrics
  • Real-time updates based on user input

🔁 Where to Go From Here

  • Integrate machine learning models for sales forecasting
  • Incorporate real-time data feeds for live analytics
  • Expand dashboard to include customer segmentation and personalization features
  • Deploy the dashboard using cloud services for scalability

Now, let's proceed with the implementation.

# multi_modal_retail_analytics_dashboard.py

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotly.express as px
import dash
from dash import dcc, html
from dash.dependencies import Input, Output
from datetime import datetime

# Load dataset
df: pd.DataFrame = pd.read_excel('online_retail_II.xlsx', sheet_name='Year 2010-2011')

# Data preprocessing
df.dropna(inplace=True)
df['InvoiceDate'] = pd.to_datetime(df['InvoiceDate'])
df['TotalPrice'] = df['Quantity'] * df['UnitPrice']

# Initialize Dash app
app = dash.Dash(__name__)
app.title = 'Retail Analytics Dashboard'

# Layout
app.layout = html.Div([
    html.H1('Multi-Modal Retail Analytics Dashboard'),
    html.Div([
        html.Label('Select Date Range:'),
        dcc.DatePickerRange(
            id='date-range',
            min_date_allowed=df['InvoiceDate'].min(),
            max_date_allowed=df['InvoiceDate'].max(),
            start_date=df['InvoiceDate'].min(),
            end_date=df['InvoiceDate'].max()
        ),
        html.Label('Select Country:'),
        dcc.Dropdown(
            id='country-dropdown',
            options=[{'label': c, 'value': c} for c in df['Country'].unique()],
            value='United Kingdom'
        )
    ], style={'width': '25%', 'display': 'inline-block', 'verticalAlign': 'top'}),
    html.Div([
        dcc.Graph(id='sales-trend'),
        dcc.Graph(id='top-products'),
        dcc.Graph(id='inventory-turnover'),
        dcc.Graph(id='marketing-effectiveness')
    ], style={'width': '70%', 'display': 'inline-block', 'padding': '0 20'})
])

# Callbacks
@app.callback(
    [Output('sales-trend', 'figure'),
     Output('top-products', 'figure'),
     Output('inventory-turnover', 'figure'),
     Output('marketing-effectiveness', 'figure')],
    [Input('date-range', 'start_date'),
     Input('date-range', 'end_date'),
     Input('country-dropdown', 'value')]
)
def update_dashboard(start_date: str, end_date: str, country: str):
    mask = (df['InvoiceDate'] >= start_date) & (df['InvoiceDate'] <= end_date) & (df['Country'] == country)
    filtered_df = df.loc[mask]

    # Sales Trend
    sales_trend = filtered_df.groupby('InvoiceDate')['TotalPrice'].sum().reset_index()
    fig_sales_trend = px.line(sales_trend, x='InvoiceDate', y='TotalPrice', title='Sales Over Time')

    # Top Products
    top_products = filtered_df.groupby('Description')['TotalPrice'].sum().nlargest(10).reset_index()
    fig_top_products = px.bar(top_products, x='Description', y='TotalPrice', title='Top 10 Products')

    # Inventory Turnover
    inventory = filtered_df.groupby('StockCode')['Quantity'].sum().reset_index()
    inventory['TurnoverRate'] = inventory['Quantity'] / (end_date - start_date).days
    fig_inventory_turnover = px.bar(inventory.nlargest(10, 'TurnoverRate'), x='StockCode', y='TurnoverRate', title='Inventory Turnover Rates')

    # Marketing Effectiveness (Placeholder for actual marketing data)
    marketing = pd.DataFrame({
        'Campaign': ['Email', 'Social Media', 'TV', 'Radio'],
        'ROI': np.random.rand(4) * 100
    })
    fig_marketing_effectiveness = px.bar(marketing, x='Campaign', y='ROI', title='Marketing Campaign Effectiveness')

    return fig_sales_trend, fig_top_products, fig_inventory_turnover, fig_marketing_effectiveness

# Run app
if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run_server(debug=True)

This implementation provides a robust foundation for a multi-modal retail analytics dashboard. You can further enhance it by integrating machine learning models for predictive analytics, incorporating real-time data streams, and deploying it on cloud platforms for broader accessibility.
